result.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control
result.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are widely deployed, yet the internal mechanisms behind their safety behavior remain poorly understood. We present a lightweight inference-time framework for localizing and manipulating safety-sensitive representations in frozen VLMs, without retraining or modifying parameters. On Qwen3-VL-4B, layer-wise activation divergence analysis reveals non-uniform safety geometry across depth. Causal interventions show that early vision layers support strong bidirectional refusal control through activation steering along a learned safety direction, with unsafe rejection spanning 6%-96%, whereas later layers respond more to activation magnitude scaling and exhibit a substantial safety-selectivity trade-off. Deeper layers remain well separated along the safety direction yet are largely insensitive to steering, distinguishing representational separability from causal controllability. InternVL2.5-4B shows qualitatively similar depth-dependent activation geometry despite differences in layer location and magnitude. Our results expose a white-box, representation-level refusal-bypass attack surface in VLM vision encoders and motivate inference-time stabilization of safety-sensitive representations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出免重训的推理期框架，通过逐层激活差异分析与沿学习到的安全方向的激活引导，在 Qwen3-VL-4B 和 InternVL2.5-4B 上定位并双向操控视觉层的拒答行为，发现安全几何随深度非均匀分布，且表示可分性与因果可控性并不同步。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按深度做因果干预、区分表示可分与因果可控」的探测思路可供核查：或可用于判断 LVR 中视觉证据在哪些层被保留、又在哪些层真正影响输出；但研究对象是安全拒答而非多模态推理，迁移需自行验证。
